title: Reconsidering Decisions to Retain Medication Safeguards After Nurses Report Hazards
content: After a nurse reports a medication hazard, a hospital may judge that an existing safeguard is sufficient. This critical narrative review used targeted searches of PubMed and Europe PMC, supplemented by citation and policy searches, to examine how published evaluations documented such decisions and their follow-up. Seven of 16 full-text evaluations described case responses or action statuses that left any decision to retain a specified safeguard undetermined. Nine examined proposed or introduced measures. One hospital programme linked nurses’ reports of barcode scanning problems to pharmacy follow-up and tracked scanning compliance. In another evaluation, a later audit identified lapses in newly introduced safeguards and prompted proposals to strengthen them. None traced a reasoned judgement of sufficiency through a later finding and reassessment to verified access to a reply by the original nurse. The studies leave the frequency of such decisions and reassessments undetermined. A future comparison could test whether an explicit invitation encourages the original nurse to return with a corroborated new observation about the same decision when access to review is the same in both groups.
